stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that watched the aggressive adult
The group that watched the quiet adult

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that studied in six short sessions
The group that studied in one long session

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group on the waiting list

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They hypothesized that the type of pill would affect anxiety.

**Participants.** The sample was 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

**Results.** The group that took the new drug: mean anxiety score = 14. The group that took the placebo: mean anxiety score = 22. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?**

**Source A.** In a study of 350 adults, the number of stressful life events in the past year correlated with the number of colds in that year (r = +0.33). Adults who reported sleeping less tended to report both more stress and more colds.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 84 office workers were randomly assigned to practice mindfulness meditation or to listen to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day. After eight weeks, the meditation group had a mean cortisol level of 9.8 nmol/L and the audiobook group 13.5 nmol/L (p = 0.02).

**Source C.** Researchers followed 500 people for a year after a major flood. Those who reported strong support from family and friends had fewer symptoms of illness and depression than those who reported little support.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it?

options.why: Correct. The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.
The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.
Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.
The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.

questions.explanation: The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an achievement test?

options.text: A test that measures what a person has already learned
options.why: Correct. This is what an achievement test means.

options.text: The belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning
options.why: That describes a growth mindset.

options.text: The boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped
options.why: That describes stereotype lift.

options.text: The belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed
options.why: That describes a fixed mindset.

questions.explanation: An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.

questions.stem: A researcher asks whether a shy three-year-old will still be shy at thirty. Which theme of developmental psychology is this?

options.why: Continuous development is the view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp.
Discontinuous development is the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase.
Correct. Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.
Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.

questions.explanation: Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.

questions.stem: A company hires a psychologist to improve the way it selects employees and to raise job satisfaction. Which kind of psychologist is this?

options.why: The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
Correct. An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.explanation: An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the score that occurs most often?

options.why: Correct. The mode is the score that occurs most often.
The normal curve is the symmetrical, bell-shaped distribution in which most scores fall near the mean.
The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.explanation: The mode is the score that occurs most often.

questions.stem: A child cannot solve a puzzle alone but can solve it with a few hints from a teacher. In Vygotsky's theory, this puzzle falls within which of the following?

options.why: Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.
Correct. The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.

questions.explanation: The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.

questions.stem: A patient describes the death of his mother in a monotone voice with no expression on his face. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.
Correct. Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.

questions.explanation: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sublimation?

options.text: The defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses
options.why: That describes reaction formation.

options.text: The defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development
options.why: That describes regression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities
options.why: Correct. This is what sublimation means.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them?

options.why: Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.
The social clock is a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement.
Correct. The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.

questions.explanation: The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes imprinting?

options.text: The movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping
options.why: That describes gross motor skills.

options.text: The process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see
options.why: Correct. This is what imprinting means.

options.text: A harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus
options.why: That describes a teratogen.

options.text: A limited time early in life when certain experiences must occur for normal development
options.why: That describes a critical period.

questions.explanation: Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes informed consent?

options.text: The requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible
options.why: That describes protection from harm.

options.text: The agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent
options.why: That describes informed assent.

options.text: The agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves
options.why: Correct. This is what informed consent means.

options.text: The explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends
options.why: That describes debriefing.

questions.explanation: Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.

questions.stem: Which neurotransmitter is the main excitatory messenger in the brain, with too much of it able to overstimulate the brain and trigger seizures?

options.why: Correct. Glutamate is the brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory.
Norepinephrine is the neurotransmitter that helps control alertness and arousal.
Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.

questions.explanation: Glutamate is the brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: A poll about internet use is carried out only online, so people without internet access cannot take part. Which problem is this?

options.why: A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.
Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.
Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.
Correct. Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.

questions.explanation: Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound?

options.why: Correct. Frequency theory is the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound.
Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.

questions.explanation: Frequency theory is the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the general adaptation syndrome?

options.text: The first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated
options.why: That describes the alarm reaction.

options.text: The second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor
options.why: That describes the resistance phase.

options.text: Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion
options.why: Correct. This is what the general adaptation syndrome means.

options.text: The third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely
options.why: That describes the exhaustion phase.

questions.explanation: The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.stem: Raccoons trained to drop coins into a box began rubbing the coins together as if washing food, despite getting no reward for it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.
Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.
Correct. Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.

questions.explanation: Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.

questions.stem: A fifteen-year-old debates what would happen to society if people could live forever. Which of Piaget's stages allows this hypothetical thinking?

options.why: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.
The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
Correct. The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.explanation: The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.stem: With a blocked nose, Jo finds that her favorite food has almost no flavor. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.
Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.
The just-noticeable difference is the smallest difference between two stimuli that a person can detect half of the time.
Correct. Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.

questions.explanation: Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an agonist?

options.text: A drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors
options.why: That describes an antagonist.

options.text: A drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption
options.why: That describes a reuptake inhibitor.

options.text: A drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it
options.why: Correct. This is what an agonist means.

options.text: The unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug
options.why: That describes withdrawal.

questions.explanation: An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: A researcher claims that dreams have no hidden meaning; the cortex simply builds a story out of random signals from the brainstem. Which theory is this?

options.why: Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
Correct. The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.

questions.explanation: The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it?

options.why: Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Correct. Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.explanation: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.stem: Positive psychologists group gratitude, hope, humor and spirituality under which virtue?

options.why: Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.
Correct. Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.
Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.
Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.

questions.explanation: Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.

questions.stem: A car crash damages a driver's spinal cord. Which part of the nervous system has been injured?

options.why: The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
Correct. The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.
The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.

questions.explanation: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: Before her driving test, Hana feels confident that she can pass because she has practiced well. This belief is which of the following?

options.why: Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.
Correct. Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.

questions.explanation: Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an eclectic approach?

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: That describes comorbidity.

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: Correct. This is what an eclectic approach means.

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: That describes the biopsychosocial model.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: That describes the diathesis-stress model.

questions.explanation: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: When Paul feels sad, he mostly remembers the disappointments in his life. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Mood-congruent memory is the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.
Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.
Context-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned.

questions.explanation: Mood-congruent memory is the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: Score on a timed reasoning test
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of years since leaving school
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the structure that processes fear and aggression?

options.why: The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
Correct. The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.explanation: The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.stem: A psychologist says a client's depression comes from his habit of interpreting every setback as proof that he is worthless. Which perspective is this?

options.why: The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.
Correct. The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.
The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.
The biological perspective is the view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes.

questions.explanation: The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.

questions.stem: After spinning on a ride, Zoe feels dizzy because the fluid in her inner ear is still moving. Which sense is affected?

options.why: Correct. The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.explanation: The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.stem: People asked to hold a pen between their teeth, which forces a smile, rate cartoons as funnier. This finding supports which of the following?

options.why: Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.
A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.
Correct. The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.
Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.explanation: The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.65. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Students who study thirty minutes a day for a week remember more a month later than students who study for the same total time in one night. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.
The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
Correct. The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.

questions.explanation: The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

options.text: The number of other people present
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: No matter how hard she tries, Zara cannot remember anything from before she was three. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.

questions.explanation: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.

questions.stem: Dee cannot stop thinking that her hands are covered in germs. This repeated, unwanted thought is which of the following?

options.why: A compulsion is a repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety.
Posttraumatic stress disorder is the disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event.
Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.
Correct. An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.

questions.explanation: An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.

questions.stem: The phone group missed more road signs. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Phone use caused the difference in attention to the road
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: Phone use and attention to the road are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people?

options.why: Correct. An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true.
The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.
Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.

questions.explanation: An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse?

options.why: Correct. Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.
Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.
The action potential is the brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires.
The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.explanation: Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.

questions.stem: A researcher who expects a drug to work smiles more at the patients who receive it and rates their improvement more generously. Which bias is this?

options.why: Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.
Correct. Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.explanation: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second?

options.why: Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.
Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.
Correct. Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.
Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.

questions.explanation: Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.50. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that working memory span causes a change in reading comprehension score?

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: The gratitude group reported higher life satisfaction. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The type of journal caused the difference in subjective well-being
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The type of journal and subjective well-being are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Leo believes he is superior to everyone, expects constant admiration and has no interest in other people's feelings. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Correct. Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.
Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.
Borderline personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior.

questions.explanation: Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.

questions.stem: After learning Spanish this year, Otto finds he can no longer remember the French words he learned last year. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.
Correct. Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.
The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.
The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.

questions.explanation: Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning?

options.why: The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
Correct. The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.
The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.

questions.stem: After a high test score, Sue says she is clever; after a low score, she says the test was unfair. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.
The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
Correct. The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.
A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.

questions.explanation: The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.

questions.stem: A patient with severe depression that has not responded to drugs is anesthetized and given a brief electric current that causes a short seizure. Which treatment is this?

options.why: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.
Correct. Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.
A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.
Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.

questions.explanation: Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.

questions.stem: Before the study could begin, a committee at the university reviewed the plan to make sure the children would be protected from harm. What is this committee called?

options.why: That is a discussion group used to collect opinions.
A confederate is someone who secretly works for the researcher.
That is a comparison condition.
Correct. An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.

questions.stem: When a dog lunges at him, Evan's heart pounds and his muscles tense, ready for him to run or defend himself. Which response to stress is this?

options.why: Correct. The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.
The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.
Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.
Distress is the negative stress that harms well-being and performance.

questions.explanation: The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands?

options.why: Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.
Correct. Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.
Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.

questions.explanation: Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.

questions.stem: Flat affect, loss of motivation and social withdrawal involve the absence of normal behaviors. Which kind of symptom are they?

options.why: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.
Correct. A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

questions.explanation: A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.

questions.stem: In a photo, two identical cars appear, and the one that looks smaller is judged to be farther away. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Correct. Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.
Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.
Convergence is the binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object.
Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.

questions.explanation: Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: +0.20, +0.35, −0.86, +0.70. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: +0.20 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.86 is farthest from zero.
+0.35 is closer to zero.
+0.70 is closer to zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.86 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: The group that was promised a certificate later spent less time drawing. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: An expected reward caused the difference in intrinsic motivation to draw
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: An expected reward and intrinsic motivation to draw are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: For three years, Otto has felt low and tired on most days, though he still manages to work. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Correct. Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.explanation: Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the conditioned response?

options.text: In classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning
options.why: That describes the unconditioned stimulus.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus
options.why: That describes the unconditioned response.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus
options.why: Correct. This is what the conditioned response means.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus
options.why: That describes the conditioned stimulus.

questions.explanation: The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the animals to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Leah is sure a fact is true but cannot remember whether she read it in a textbook or saw it in a film. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Correct. Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.

questions.explanation: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a pheromone?

options.text: A person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely
options.why: That describes a supertaster.

options.text: The sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first
options.why: That describes olfaction.

options.text: The sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus
options.why: That describes gustation.

options.text: A chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others
options.why: Correct. This is what a pheromone means.

questions.explanation: A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the one-word stage?

options.text: The applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'
options.why: That describes overgeneralization.

options.text: The vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months
options.why: That describes cooing.

options.text: The stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'
options.why: That describes babbling.

options.text: The stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words
options.why: Correct. This is what the one-word stage means.

questions.explanation: The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes denial?

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: That describes projection.

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: That describes displacement.

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: That describes rationalization.

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: Correct. This is what denial means.

questions.explanation: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.

questions.stem: Mila constantly seeks out unfamiliar music, foreign films and trips to places she has never been. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Correct. Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.explanation: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes?

options.why: In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Correct. Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.

questions.explanation: Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The amount of caffeine consumed each day
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of anxiety

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of anxiety.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Anxiety was defined as each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The drug group had lower anxiety scores. On average, the value was 14 for the group that took the new drug and 22 for the group that took the placebo, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The drug group had lower anxiety scores. (14 compared with 22).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the type of pill affects anxiety. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the type of pill. The finding illustrates the placebo effect: improvement caused by expectation alone, which a placebo control group measures.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Long-term stress harms health, but coping strategies and social support reduce its effects.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, people with more stressful life events had more colds in the same year (r = +0.33).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the general adaptation syndrome: prolonged stress keeps the body in the resistance phase and eventually exhausts it, which suppresses the immune system and makes illness more likely.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers who practiced mindfulness meditation had lower cortisol levels (9.8) than workers who listened to an audiobook (13.5).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through emotion-focused coping: meditation manages the emotional and physical reaction to stress, which lowers the body's stress-hormone response.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
